cases.finding: ClawArena-Team directly exercises whole-team current control through creation, privilege/workspace assignment, inspection, scheduling and dynamic workflow management, but the benchmark supplies that organization and fixed worker pool. Published manager-model results are not native canonical-harness S3 observations.

The paired experiment isolates a whole-team current-control right: the hierarchical Manager may reject completed worker output and loop work back with corrective instructions, while the flat Manager observes the same workflow but is forced to route forward. Five agents, roles, prompts, tools, model assignment and product data are otherwise held fixed. This directly exercises benchmark-defined S3 authority, but the organization is authored by the experiment and runs on LangGraph only as an execution substrate, so the published results are not native S3 observations for LangGraph or another canonical harness.

SupervisorAgent adds a meta-level runtime control relation around a base MAS: it observes live interaction state, detects high-risk current conditions, chooses approve/guidance/correction/verification actions and returns those interventions into ongoing operation. The published Smolagent pass@1 comparison reports the same 50.91% average GAIA accuracy while average token use falls from 527.76K to 371.12K (reported 29.68% reduction). This is admitted direct composed S3 evidence at the SMAS boundary, not native S3 evidence for Smolagent, AWorld or OAgents; the mixed intervention repertoire also prevents interpreting the aggregate gain as an isolated S3-only causal effect.

The native historical Magentic-One orchestrator ablation removes whole-team ledgers, progress tracking, planning/replanning, loop detection and explicit direction and changes end-task performance. The benchmarks do not isolate S3 and the ablation spans both S2 and S3, so it remains proxy evidence. Numeric results live only in the shared raw observation record.

Canonical LLaMAR establishes S3=A through its whole-team planner/current-control loop. The first-party 2-agent MAP-THOR Table 3 ablation changes Planner/Verifier/Corrector combinations and moves broad task SR/TR/C/B outcomes, so it is native S3-relevant capability evidence. It is not direct S3 evidence because the benchmark targets end-task performance and the ablation does not isolate one S3 current-control right; the exact Git execution revision is also not identified by the paper. Numeric results live only in the shared raw observation record.

EnterpriseArena stresses scarce-resource allocation under uncertainty, an S3-relevant current-control capability, but the CFO-style benchmark environment blends current regulation with prospective reasoning and does not exercise a canonical harness control plane.

This is a strong matched framework experiment: Gemini 2.5 Flash, tools, workload and most prompts are fixed while the orchestration framework varies. It still does not exercise the canonical S3 implementations: Agno is run in TeamMode.coordinate rather than the TeamMode.tasks path that establishes canonical S3=A, and AutoGen is run through SelectorGroupChat rather than MagenticOneOrchestrator. CrewAI and LangGraph are current S3=— negative controls. Fixed-model framework parity therefore does not make this a matched native-S3 comparison.

PrincipalBench measures decomposition, failure detection, adversarial recovery and context coherence, but its benchmark harness creates the worker outputs with WorkerSimulator, injects failures and presents the resulting outputs to one model through a benchmark-defined principal prompt. It does not exercise a canonical harness's native worker lifecycle, live assignment, resource/priority authority, retry/replan or whole-system control implementation, so it remains S3-adjacent scaffolded proxy evidence.

Canonical Multi-Agent Orchestration establishes S3=A from its standard live-state supervisor. Its first-party deterministic benchmark directly ablates that native supervisor path against the same engine using only HeuristicRouter while retry and parallelism remain disabled in both clean comparison arms. Published results move from 11/54 passed and 56.7% routing accuracy to 48/54 passed and 100% routing accuracy. This is admitted direct native S3 evidence; the separately retry-enabled recovery arm is outside the clean supervisor-only attribution, and the embedded historical run SHA is no longer publicly resolvable.

Canonical Omnigent already establishes S3=A at review ref 4d963a36. A later merged first-party recovery path observes a current-control disturbance after parent-runner loss, distinguishes unfinished child commitments from completed/stopped/foreign/live-elsewhere work, rebinds eligible interrupted children under their original identities and resumes those commitments without creating replacement workers. PR #7662 reports dedicated regression coverage and a real Polly/Codex crash-and-Retry witness preserving the same child and dispatch identities. This is admitted descriptive canonical S3 evidence at a post-assessment descendant revision; it is not relabeled as evidence at the earlier assessment ref and is not materially matched to the Multi-Agent Orchestration ablation.

OrchestraBench directly studies routing, injected orchestration failures, cascade radius and recovery in controlled dependency chains, which makes its protocol highly relevant to S3 current-control capability. The reviewed public evidence is a benchmark-defined orchestration organization and no authoritative code source was recovered that links its measurements to native canonical harness S3 implementations, so it cannot populate the primary baseline today.

Canonical C.A.D.I.S. establishes S3=A(P) through a current whole-agent awareness path with model-owned child-agent commitment plus shipped parent list/kill/cancel intervention controls. The reviewed benchmark/result surfaces are local performance measurements rather than whole-runtime current-control intervention experiments, so no direct native S3 capability observation is admitted.

cases.benchmark: Awaken native run-control and recovery path
cases.finding: Canonical Awaken establishes S3=C(P) through first-party run-control, cancellation/resume and recovery surfaces. The repository exposes tests and mechanism documentation but no committed capability result that isolates a current-control intervention and measures its effect on subsequent whole-system operation, so this admission does not add a direct S3 observation.

Canonical ARES establishes S3=C(P) through constructor current-control/scheduler surfaces. Its committed scheduler and fabric benchmarks measure microperformance rather than a controlled current-control intervention and resulting organizational outcome, so no direct native S3 capability observation is admitted.
